summary: Kengo Harimoto is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University and completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass in 1999. He held posts at Mahidol University (attested 2020) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2022).
Kenji Ishii is a religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1973 to 1982 and held a post at Kokugakuin University from circa 1988 to 2020.
Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University under Seizan Yanagida.

Kenji Matsuo is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1975 to 1985 and served at Yamagata University from circa 1989 to 2019.
Kenji Shimada (1917–2000) was a Sinology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1938 to 1941 and later worked there as a researcher from circa 1950 to 1981.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indology scholar. He studied at Leiden University (2015–2016) and under supervisors including Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter Bisschop. He held a fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II from 2019 to 2021.

Kenju Kasahara (1851–1883) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, and learned under Friedrich Max Müller (1879–1882) and Arthur Anthony Macdonell (circa 1880–1882).
Kenjuro Yanagida (1893–1983) was a philosophy scholar. He studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida circa 1922–1925, later holding a post at Hirosaki University.
Kennard Lipman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Günther and served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

Kenneth Adrian Raine Kennedy (1930–2014) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1949 to 1962 and held a post at Cornell University from circa 1964 to 2005.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University (attested 2007).

Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned an M.A. at UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. at Australian National University. His academic posts include Eastern Michigan University, UCLA, UC Madison, University of Toronto, and the University of Copenhagen.

Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Columbia University, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY Graduate Center (PhD) under Aloysius Pieris. He held teaching posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara. From circa 1921 to 1935, he served as a professor at the Pacific School of Religion and lecturer at the University of California.

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He served as a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research and the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism (1996–1999).

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Stanford, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held faculty posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1984–1987) and Musashino University (1998–2014).
Kenneth R. Valpey is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held a post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth Roy Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Downing College, Cambridge, he served on Cambridge's Faculty of Oriental Studies (circa 1951–1992) and was president of the Pali Text Society (1981–1994).

Kenneth de Burgh Codrington (1899–1986) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and Wadham College, and held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (circa 1923–1948) and the University of London (circa 1948–1965).

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Aichi Gakuin University (2000–2010), the University of Tokyo (professor from 2010), and Rissho University (professor in 2025).
